\textbf{(a)} Let $u=t^3$, $du=3t^2dt$, so $t^5dt=\frac13u\,du$:
\[\frac13\int u\sin u\,du=\frac13\big(-u\cos u+\sin u\big)+C=\boxed{-\tfrac13t^3\cos(t^3)+\tfrac13\sin(t^3)+C}\]
(by parts with $w=u$, $dv=\sin u\,du$).

\textbf{(b)} Let $u=\sqrt x$, $x=u^2$, $dx=2u\,du$:
\[\int\frac{2u\,du}{u^2(u^2+u)}=\int\frac{2\,du}{u^2(u+1)}=\int\Big(-\frac2u+\frac2{u^2}+\frac2{u+1}\Big)du=-2\ln u-\frac2u+2\ln(u+1)+C.\]
\[\boxed{2\ln\Big(\frac{\sqrt x+1}{\sqrt x}\Big)-\frac{2}{\sqrt x}+C}\]
2:
\textbf{(a)} By parts, $u=\ln(1+t^2)$, $dv=dt$:
\[\Big[t\ln(1+t^2)\Big]_0^1-\int_0^1\frac{2t^2}{1+t^2}dt=\ln2-\int_0^1\Big(2-\frac{2}{1+t^2}\Big)dt=\boxed{\ln2-2+\frac\pi2}\approx0.264.\]
\textbf{(b)} Let $u=4+x^2$, $du=2x\,dx$, $x^2=u-4$; $u$ runs from 4 to 8:
\[\frac12\int_4^8\frac{u-4}{\sqrt u}du=\frac12\Big[\tfrac23u^{3/2}-8u^{1/2}\Big]_4^8=\frac12\Big[\Big(\tfrac{32\sqrt2}{3}-16\sqrt2\Big)-\Big(\tfrac{16}{3}-16\Big)\Big]=\boxed{\frac{16-8\sqrt2}{3}}\approx1.562.\]
3:
The integrand blows up at both $x=0$ and $x=1$. Substitute $x=\sin^2\theta$, $dx=2\sin\theta\cos\theta\,d\theta$, $\sqrt{x(1-x)}=\sin\theta\cos\theta$ ($0\le\theta\le\frac\pi2$):
\[\int_0^1\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x(1-x)}}=\lim\int\frac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}d\theta=\int_0^{\pi/2}2\,d\theta=\pi.\]
The integral \textbf{converges} to \boxed{\pi}.
4:
$v(t)=3t^2-12=3(t-2)(t+2)$ is negative on $[0,2)$ and positive after $t=2$. Total distance $=\int_0^b|v|\,dt$:
\[\int_0^2(12-3t^2)dt+\int_2^b(3t^2-12)dt=\big[12t-t^3\big]_0^2+\big[t^3-12t\big]_2^b=16+(b^3-12b+16).\]
\[\boxed{b^3-12b+32}\]
5:
The triangle is bounded by $y=0$, the line through $(0,1),(1,0)$ ($x=1-y$, or $y=1-x$) and the line through $(0,1),(2,0)$ ($x=2-2y$, or $y=1-\frac x2$). For $0\le y\le1$ it runs from $x=1-y$ to $x=2-2y$.

\textbf{(a) Washers} (horizontal slices, axis $x=-1$): outer radius $(2-2y)+1$, inner radius $(1-y)+1$:
\[V=\int_0^1\pi\Big[(3-2y)^2-(2-y)^2\Big]dy.\]
\textbf{(b) Shells} (vertical slices, radius $x+1$). For $0\le x\le1$ the height is $(1-\frac x2)-(1-x)=\frac x2$; for $1\le x\le2$ it is $1-\frac x2$:
\[V=\int_0^12\pi(x+1)\frac x2\,dx+\int_1^22\pi(x+1)\Big(1-\frac x2\Big)dx.\]
(Both equal $2\pi$.)
6:
\textbf{(a)} A horizontal slice at height $y$ is a disk of radius $x=\sqrt{\sin^{-1}y}$, so its area is $\pi x^2=\pi\sin^{-1}y$. It weighs $40\pi\sin^{-1}y\,dy$ lb and is lifted $1-y$ ft to the top:
\[W=\int_0^140\pi\sin^{-1}(y)\,(1-y)\,dy.\]
\textbf{(b)} $\int_0^1\sin^{-1}y\,dy=\big[y\sin^{-1}y+\sqrt{1-y^2}\big]_0^1=\frac\pi2-1$. By parts, $\int_0^1y\sin^{-1}y\,dy=\Big[\frac{y^2}{2}\sin^{-1}y\Big]_0^1-\frac12\int_0^1\frac{y^2}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}dy=\frac\pi4-\frac12\cdot\frac\pi4=\frac\pi8$. So
\[W=40\pi\Big(\frac\pi2-1-\frac\pi8\Big)=\boxed{15\pi^2-40\pi}\approx22.38\ \text{ft-lb}.\]
8:
Area $A=\frac{\pi r^2}{4}$. The moment about the $y$-axis:
\[\int_0^rx\sqrt{r^2-x^2}\,dx=\Big[-\tfrac13(r^2-x^2)^{3/2}\Big]_0^r=\frac{r^3}{3}.\]
\[\bar x=\frac{r^3/3}{\pi r^2/4}=\boxed{\frac{4r}{3\pi}}.\]

Separate (divide by $e^{-\tan y}\cos^2y$):
\[\int e^{\tan y}\sec^2y\,dy=\int2x\,dx\ \Rightarrow\ e^{\tan y}=x^2+C.\]
$y(0)=\frac\pi4$: $e^{1}=C$. So $\tan y=\ln(x^2+e)$ and
\[\boxed{y=\tan^{-1}\!\big(\ln(x^2+e)\big)}.\]
10:
\textbf{(a)} Linear equation $y'-\frac{1}{20}y=-A$. The equilibrium is $y=20A$; the general solution is $y=20A+Ce^{t/20}$. $y(0)=20000\Rightarrow C=20000-20A$:
\[\boxed{y(t)=20A+(20000-20A)e^{t/20}}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $y(10)=0$: $20A+(20000-20A)e^{1/2}=0\Rightarrow 20A(e^{1/2}-1)=20000e^{1/2}$:
\[\boxed{A=\frac{1000\sqrt e}{\sqrt e-1}}\approx\$2541.49\ \text{per year}.\]
